privacy.heading: What the dashboard keeps, and where
privacy.intro: A short notice before reader mode’s first use, always available in its Settings.
privacy.phoneText: Reader mode keeps the statements teachers hand you encrypted in this browser, with a key sealed under a passphrase of its own. Nobody can recover a forgotten passphrase: this PC must then be erased.
privacy.readerText: It opens the statements teachers hand you as files, on this PC, checks their signatures here, and connects to nothing.
privacy.siteText: The dashboard loads from https://minhajna-admin.djazair.dev at each visit, with no offline copy and no update check. Cloudflare serves it and sees this PC’s IP address and browser at each visit, under its own policy. The project keeps no access logs.
privacy.directoryTitle: The directory pages connect, with made-up data only
privacy.directoryText: The Ministry’s list and a school’s pages send what you enter in them, with each page’s edit code, to the project’s demo server, https://minhajna-demo.djazair.dev. The server keeps what you enter in the clear, outside any demo world, and each edit code only as its hash. Cloudflare, in front of it, sees your IP address; the server keeps no address beyond its rate limits’ counts. Enter made-up data only, until the national system exists.
privacy.trackingText: No ads, no analytics, no record of hours or location. Crash reports stay off until you turn them on in reader mode’s Settings. A report is then kept on this PC, unencrypted, until you send it, or choose not to, on reader mode’s home, and leaves this PC only if you share it: through the browser’s share menu, or copied for you to paste yourself.
privacy.eraseText: “Erase this PC”, in reader mode’s Settings or from its lock page when the passphrase is forgotten, removes everything reader mode keeps in this browser, and the dashboard’s language with it.
privacy.publisherText: The open-source Minhajna project, which serves the dashboard’s files and runs the demo server. It receives nothing reader mode keeps.
privacy.rightsText: To see what the project holds about you, and to have it corrected and deleted within 10 days.
privacy.fileLine: This PC uses no camera. A statement opens through the browser’s file dialog, which gives the dashboard no access to your other files.

connections.title: What the dashboard connects to, and why
connections.site: The dashboard connects to its own address, https://minhajna-admin.djazair.dev, for its files at each visit. It keeps no offline copy and looks for no update. Cloudflare serves it and sees this PC’s IP address and browser; the project keeps no access logs.
connections.directory: The directory pages connect to the demo server, https://minhajna-demo.djazair.dev, to read and save the Ministry’s list and a school’s book, with each page’s edit code. The server keeps what you enter in the clear, made up until the national system exists, and each edit code only as its hash. Cloudflare, in front of it, sees this PC’s IP address; the server keeps no address beyond its rate limits’ counts.
connections.reader: Reader mode connects to nothing. Statements come in as files you pick through the browser’s file dialog, which gives the dashboard no access to your other files.
connections.crashReport: A crash report, if you turned crash reports on, is shown in full on reader mode’s home and leaves this PC only when you choose to share it: through the browser’s share menu, or copied for you to paste where it has none. It holds the error’s type, where it happened in the code, the version and the names of the last screens opened, without the error’s message or any content.
connections.register: Any connection the project adds is listed in the NETWORK.md file of the source code, with what is sent and why, before it reaches the dashboard.
